test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 17 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is INCORRECT with respect to repo rate?

options.text: It is a single policy rate to signal the stance of monetary policy to achieve macro-economic objectives of growth with price stability
It is a policy rate which is the key lending rate of the central bank, and its nomenclature varies from country to country.
It is the rate at which banks place their funds with the RBI and receive collateral.
It is the rate at which the commercial banks borrow funds from the RBI.

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The repo rate is a single policy rate used by central banks to signal the stance of monetary policy to achieve macro-economic objectives of growth with price stability.

• The repo rate is a key lending rate of the central bank, and its nomenclature varies from country to country.

• The repo rate is the rate at which commercial banks borrow funds from the RBI (Reserve Bank of India).

• The incorrect statement is that the repo rate is the rate at which banks place their funds with the RBI and receive collateral. This describes the reverse repo rate, not the repo rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Repo Rate:**

• The repo rate, or repurchase rate, is the rate at which the central bank of a country (RBI in India) lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.

• The repo rate is used by monetary authorities to control inflation. When inflation is high, central banks increase the repo rate to discourage banks from borrowing, which reduces the money supply in the economy.

• Conversely, when the central bank wants to inject funds into the system, it lowers the repo rate, making borrowing cheaper for banks.

• It is a crucial instrument of monetary policy and is used to maintain liquidity and control inflation in the economy.

• **Reverse Repo Rate:**

• It is the rate at which the central bank borrows money from commercial banks within the country.

• It is a monetary policy instrument which can be used to control the money supply in the country.

• The reverse repo rate is an instrument to absorb the liquidity in the market, thereby tightening the money supply.

• When the reverse repo rate is increased, it encourages banks to park their surplus funds with the central bank, thus absorbing excess liquidity from the banking system.

• **Monetary Policy:**

• Monetary policy refers to the policy adopted by the monetary authority of a country to control either the interest rate payable on very short-term borrowing or the money supply.

• It is a key tool used to achieve macroeconomic objectives such as controlling inflation, consumption, growth, and liquidity.

• In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is responsible for formulating and implementing monetary policy.

• Key instruments of monetary policy include the repo rate, reverse repo rate, cash reserve ratio (CRR), and statutory liquidity ratio (SLR).
